info.title: Kit Taxi Driver API
info.description: Every request and response here was recorded from a running server. Each response lists every key seen in any recorded call, with nullable marked, so nothing is lost on import.

get.description:
Everything the app needs before its first screen paints, and the only call it can make without a token.

Serves the sign-in screen end to end:
• branding — wordmark, logo, the map behind the welcome copy, and the headline text, so wording changes need no app release
• theme — colours, corner radii and typefaces as tokens rather than values hard-coded in the app
• auth.methods — drives the Phone / Email toggle. One entry means the app shows no toggle
• auth.countries — the GB +44 picker, with preselected saying which one it opens on
• auth.social — Apple and Google. A disabled provider is omitted rather than returned as enabled:false, so the app renders what it is given and decides nothing
• legal — the two footer links, each with a version that is sent back on acceptance so consent is auditable

Cacheable for five minutes; it changes on deploy, not per request.

post.description:
Checks the details and sends a code, and returns nothing but success. Nothing is written to a driver yet: the details ride on the code, so a form nobody finishes leaves no account behind, and nobody can rewrite an account they have not proved they own.

gender is optional, one of MALE, FEMALE or OTHER, and is stored as the driver's word rather than a checked fact: it shows on their profile and cannot switch gender-specific riding on. Approving their application confirms it, because that is when somebody has read the identity document — see 14 · Ride preferences.

Proves the code. On a first sign-up this is also where the account is created, from the details /signup left behind.

It returns nothing: the tokens and the driver come from GET /session, which the app calls next with the same number. A proved code is burned immediately — sending it again answers CODE_EXPIRED. Reserved test numbers always accept 1111.

get.description:
The first call after /verifyOTP. The driver holds no token yet, so the number they just verified says who they are. Encode the + as %2B.

Returns the tokens, who the driver is, what they may do, and every document grouped the way the screens are. The proof it spends is one-use and lasts two minutes.

post.summary: Get a new pair of tokens
post.description:
The auth token is short-lived, so the app calls this quietly in the background rather than sending the driver back to the sign-in screen every hour. expiresIn on the session response says when to.

The proof travels in the body, not the Authorization header — by the time this is called the auth token has usually expired, so it cannot be renewed with itself. Sending an auth token here answers WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE.

Both tokens come back replaced, so a phone in regular use never reaches the refresh token's own expiry and never asks the driver to sign in again for no reason.

post.description:
The Submit button. declarationAccepted is the tick under the list; the wording belongs to the app, and the acceptance is dated against the driver here.

From this point every document is frozen — /documents, /vehicle and /review all answer APPLICATION_LOCKED — so nothing changes under a reviewer who is already reading it. canSubmit turns 0 and status turns submitted.

patch.summary: Upload every document in one call
patch.description:
Every document, every photo and the vehicle details in a single call — enough on its own to take a new driver from nothing to submittable.

The two calls above split the same thing the way the app collects it, one screen at a time. Either route ends with missingImages 0, missingValues 0 and canSubmit 1.

driverGovernmentId is the only document with a dropdown, so it is the only one needing type. passport asks for front and back; rationCard and birthCertificate ask for front alone, and sending back for those is refused as UNKNOWN_IMAGE_SLOT.

driverPrivateHireLicence is optional — leave it out and the application still submits. It is why imagesUploaded reads 15 of 13: thirteen are required, and the optional licence adds two on top.

get.description:
What the waiting screen shows. reference is what the driver quotes to support; it is issued on the first submission and kept for the life of the case, so a resubmission after a rejection is still the same one.

status is draft, submitted, rejected or approved. reviewedAt is when a reviewer last acted — the app words its own "started 2 hours ago" from it, and the copy on the screen belongs to the app throughout.

rejection is null here, because nothing has been decided yet. On an approval the home screen unlocks; on a rejection it fills in and the upload routes open back up — the next folder records that.

get.summary: Get the whole application to review
get.description:
Everything the driver is about to submit, flat: the personal details, then a row per value and a row per image with whether it is in and where to look at it.

This screen only displays and corrects, so the placeholders, choices and helper text the upload screens need are left out. url is what the eye button opens, and is null until the image is uploaded.

missingImages and missingValues are what the Submit button waits on; canSubmit turns 1 when both reach zero. An optional document is listed but never counted. Ticking the declaration is the app's own gate on top of canSubmit.

200.description: Get the whole application to review

Get_the_whole_application_to_review.summary: Get the whole application to review

get.description:
One call for a screen whose values live in four places — the driver, their vehicle, their documents and their week. Only the value each row shows travels; the labels beside them belong to the app.

totalRides is counted from the rides themselves. There is a drivers.total_rides column and nothing maintains it, so it is not used.

renewsOn and documentsExpiringCount come from the expiry fields the document config marks as a month, measured against application.documentExpiryWarningDays.

rating is always null: nothing produces one yet. It is in the response so the screen has somewhere to put a score, not because this driver has none.

gender is the one a reviewer recorded from the identity document, for the personal information row. It is null until someone has. GET /ridePreferences carries it too, with the rest of what the gender-specific riding screen needs.

post.description:
Public, because it is how the first person ever gets in. On an empty admin_users the account is activated immediately as Super Admin — there is nobody to approve it. Every account after that is created pending and cannot sign in until an existing admin approves it, which is what activated tells you.

This example shows the second case: a reviewer already exists on the development server, so the new account comes back pending and activated is false. Approve it from PATCH /admin/users/:adminId, or sign in as the reviewer below.

Passwords are at least 10 characters, and stored scrypt-hashed.

Returns the token the /admin calls send. The collection script puts it in the adminToken variable for you. expiresIn is eight hours.

A wrong address and a wrong password fail identically, as INVALID_CREDENTIALS, so neither answer says whether an account exists. An account that is not active is the one case that says more — ADMIN_PENDING_APPROVAL, ADMIN_SUSPENDED or ADMIN_REJECTED — because the person needs telling why.

get.description: The whole profile behind a row: the account, the vehicle and the documents.

patch.description:
How an admin records a gender for a driver who skipped the field at sign-up, or whose answer was wrong. It is not a gate: a driver who gave one at sign-up needs nothing from an admin.

The server stamps genderVerifiedAt as a record of when a person last checked. Nothing reads it. null clears the gender itself, which does switch the mode off — there is then nothing to match on, though the driver's stored preference stays.

One of MALE, FEMALE or OTHER. The same call also takes status, email and city; this is the whole body it needs for the gender.

driverId is whichever driver last took a session, which the collection script keeps in step with authToken — so this sets it on the driver you are signed in as.

What an admin sends when an application is nearly right. It reopens the uploads and writes the note the driver reads on their status screen.

documents is keyed the same way a PATCH /documents body is: id is the document id from GET /session. image narrows it to one photograph — front, back, left or right — and may be left out to send the whole document back. reason is required on every entry, because without it the driver gets a card telling them nothing.

The admin's name is taken from the token, never the body.

THE OTHER DECISIONS ON THIS ENDPOINT
Accept it:            { "action": "approve_application" }
Refuse it outright:   { "action": "reject_application", "reason": "…" }

approve_application needs nothing else — an approval has no note and no documents to name. Both it and reject_application are terminal: the transition table allows nothing after either, so a second decision is refused as INVALID_TRANSITION. request_changes is the only one that reopens the uploads and puts a note on the driver's status screen.

get.description:
The history screen. Rides come back newest first, already grouped into local days with a count and a total per day — which day a ride belongs to is a timezone question, and the client would need the same zone and arithmetic to make its own totals agree.

Paging is on a cursor, not an offset: send loadMoreBefore straight back as ?loadMoreBefore= and nothing is skipped or repeated if a ride is written mid-scroll. Null means there is nothing older, which is what hides "Load earlier rides".

thisWeek counts the week however far the list has been scrolled and whichever status is being looked at, because that is what the header shows.

?status=completed|cancelled is what the filter control narrows the list to. A cancelled Nothing in a ride is null. A cancellation still carries its destinationAddress and endTime, and its distanceInKm and durationInMinutes are zero rather than absent — nothing was driven. The app picks what to show by status, not by checking for nulls.

200.description: Ride history · Ride history, cancelled only

get.description:
The screen shown the moment a ride ends. totalFare, tipAmount and serviceFee are the breakdown; driverEarnings is what the driver keeps. serviceFee travels positive — the minus sign belongs to the app.

The money is stored per ride rather than recomputed, so changing the fee rate next month cannot rewrite what a driver was paid last month.

A cancellation carries waitMinutes and no distance — the wait is what earned the fee.

The earnings screen. period is today, week or month, matching its three tabs, and defaults to week.

dailyEarnings holds one bar per day in the period, zeroes included — a gap would read as missing data rather than a day off. The peak the chart marks is simply the largest of them.

percentageChangeFromLastPeriod compares with the period before this one, and is null when that period earned nothing, because the change is then not a number anything can render.

onlineTimeInMinutes is time available for work, not time on a trip: the gap between two jobs counts. It comes from driver_shifts, clipped to the period, so a shift spanning midnight counts towards both days.

Weeks run Monday to Sunday and months are calendar months, both worked out in the configured timezone rather than UTC.

patch.description:
Both fields are optional and either may be sent alone — the toggle and the choice beside it are two controls on one screen. A body with neither is refused rather than treated as a no-op, because the driver pressed save.

The response is the whole screen again, so nothing has to be re-read after a save.

A fourth refusal this run cannot show: with features.genderPreference off in the configuration, every PATCH here answers 403 GENDER_FEATURE_DISABLED, because nothing would act on what was stored.

Turning_it_on_without_a_verified_gender_.summary: Turning it on without a verified gender (403)

error.message: This driver has no gender recorded, so there is nothing to match on and gender-specific riding cannot be turned on. It is asked for at sign-up, and an admin can set one.

A_preference_that_is_not_one_of_the_thre.summary: A preference that is not one of the three (422)

get.description:
Three things decide whether this driver is matched by passenger gender, and all three have to agree: the feature is switched on for everyone, the driver has a gender recorded, and they have turned the mode on themselves.

isGenderSpecificModeOn is the answer to that whole question, not the stored toggle. Switching features.genderPreference off reads false here for every driver, while each driver's own choice stays stored and comes back by itself when the feature returns — nobody is asked to set it again.

driverGender is what the driver gave at sign-up, or what an admin set. Null is the one thing that stops the toggle, and is what the screen explains.

canTurnOnGenderSpecificMode is whether this driver may use the feature at all. The app could work it out from the fields above and should not have to — eligibility is the server's answer to give, so the rule behind it can gain a condition without an app release. A false here is what a PATCH turning the mode on would refuse.

The labels and the paragraph explaining the feature belong to the app, as everywhere else. Only this driver's state travels.
